## Findings
- claim-1: The two Theorem 5.4 families are stated to be generating sets, each of cardinality \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\), and minimality means that no proper subfamily generates. [source-6@L14-L42|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: If either known \(N\)-element generating family has quotient \(J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^N\), then its image is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis and the family is minimal.
- claim-3: For \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(\deg x=1\), and \(J=(2x,x^2)\), the homogeneous generating family \((2x,x^2)\) is minimal but \(J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2\), so minimality does not imply free integral indecomposables.
## Strategy
Let \(\mathcal F=(f_1,\ldots,f_N)\) be either known \(N\)-element generating family of \(J\), where \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\). Since \(\mathcal F\) generates \(J\), its images generate
\[
Q:=J/\Lambda_+J,
\]
so there is a surjection \(\mathbb Z^N\twoheadrightarrow Q\). If \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\), this is a surjective square integral matrix. Its determinant is therefore a unit, \(\det=\pm1\), hence the images of \(\mathcal F\) are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q\). No proper subfamily of a basis generates \(Q\); therefore no proper subfamily generates \(J\). Thus \(\mathcal F\) is minimal. This includes \(a=0\) or \(b=0\), when \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}=1\).

The converse fails. Let
\[
A=\mathbb Z[x],\qquad \deg x=1,\qquad A_+=(x),\qquad J=(2x,x^2).
\]
The homogeneous pair \((2x,x^2)\) generates \(J\), and is minimal since
\[
x^2\notin (2x),\qquad 2x\notin(x^2).
\]
Moreover,
\[
A_+J=xJ=(2x^2,x^3).
\]
Degreewise,
\[
(J/A_+J)_1=2\mathbb Zx\cong\mathbb Z,\qquad
(J/A_+J)_2=\mathbb Zx^2/2\mathbb Zx^2\cong\mathbb Z/2,
\]
and \((J/A_+J)_d=0\) for \(d\ge3\). Hence
\[
J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2,
\]
which is not free abelian and, in particular, is not \(\mathbb Z^2\).

## Gaps
None for this certificate.

## Next
This certificate is established. It proves only the stated implication and its non-converse; it does not establish the parent theorem.
